card.name: Cancer cells in explanatory passages
card.fires_on: Words in passages explaining how cancer or tumor cells grow, divide or die, mostly 'cells', 'the' or 'cell' right before 'cells' is expected.

modes.label: Before or at 'cells'
modes.description: The word 'the', 'healthy' or 'cancer' sits right before an expected 'cells' in a cancer-biology explanation.
modes.example: The main difference between cancer cells and healthy cells is that<< the>> cancer cells are multiplying uncontrollably.

modes.label: The word cells itself
modes.description: The word 'cells' or 'cell' appears in a phrase about tumor cells being killed or dying.
modes.example: programmed<< cell>> death, in colon cancer cells.

modes.label: Abnormal division wording
modes.description: Words in a definition of cancer as cells dividing without control.
modes.example: A term for diseases in which cells divide ab<<normally>> without control or order.
